doc_screened_files.reason: Directly matches the panic site in the backtrace: `lower_match_tree` and `traverse_candidate` live here, and the assertion about `leaf_candidate.false_edge_start_block.is_some()` is in this match-lowering engine. The duplicate `(!|!) if true` arms exercise never-pattern and guard handling, so this is the strongest root-cause candidate.

This module owns match-lowering utilities for false-edge emission, fake borrows, and borrow-kind conversion. That makes it a likely source of the missing `false_edge_start_block` bookkeeping that the assertion checks.
This file chooses and emits the MIR tests for match candidates. A bug in how it classifies or lowers never-pattern tests could produce a candidate without the expected false-edge start block.
It simplifies match-pair trees before test generation. A bad simplification of or-patterns or never-pattern branches could drop the guard/false-edge structure needed later by `lower_match_tree`.

This is the top-level MIR builder that wires the whole THIR-to-MIR pipeline together. If the match-lowering bug is triggered by a broader builder integration issue rather than a single helper, this is the next most plausible orchestration site.

The input pattern is lowered here before MIR match lowering sees it. A mismatch in THIR pattern lowering for never patterns or or-patterns could propagate malformed match candidates into `build/matches`.

This module validates THIR pattern and match structure. Since the reproducer uses duplicate arms with never patterns, a validation/pathology here could be feeding an unexpected shape into later lowering.

The duplicate-arm/never-pattern shape is exactly the sort of case handled by exhaustiveness and usefulness analysis. If candidate construction or witness generation is wrong here, MIR match lowering can receive inconsistent pattern structure.

This file defines the constructor-based pattern representation consumed by usefulness analysis. Corruption or misclassification of or-pattern/never-pattern structure here would affect the match candidates built upstream of MIR lowering.

It defines the constructor vocabulary used to analyze matches, including how patterns are specialized and split. Bugs here could mis-handle never patterns or or-pattern branches and lead to malformed candidate traversal later in MIR building.
